answer: Arrival Skew Gate. Each identity must complete its first N actions inside a narrow arrival window whose width shrinks as concurrent signups rise; the gate holds a knoll of admitted slots per interval, so burst registration is throttled to the observed organic rate. A sybil cluster must therefore spread signups across many intervals or pay the saffron cost of inflated dwell time and wasted capacity per puppet. The fable of cheap mass registration collapses because every extra identity now costs real elapsed time plus idle throughput, not just a fee.
